items.title: The Code of Theseus: Can Agents Rebuild Software from Recovered Design Documents?
items.abstract: LLM agents increasingly design a system before implementing it, yet the data to train and evaluate them centres on implementation and testing: requirements and design artefacts are often missing, outdated or private. Source code, in contrast, is abundant. Prior work recovers architecture documentation by feeding LLMs the source code or letting agents explore it, which saturates the context, does not scale to many repositories, and yields a single artefact rather than aligned ones. We present a framework that recovers aligned stakeholder intent, requirements and architecture from a compact repository representation, a static dependency graph and key contextual files, and release the artefacts of 10,764 Java, Python, C/C++ and C# repositories as a dataset. An LLM judge rates the artefacts of three generators as clear and internally consistent, but less reliably correct and at the right level of abstraction. To test whether the artefacts carry the design, we pose a software Ship of Theseus: a coding agent rebuilds 29 Commit0 libraries from the intent alone or with the recovered requirements and architecture, given only an interface contract and part of the tests. The artefacts do not significantly change the held-out pass rate (33.7% vs. 35.8%), but bring the rebuilt module structure significantly closer to the original (module F1 from 0.54 to 0.63), with either generator and even with concise artefacts. Recovered artefacts thus convey design that tests do not capture, offering a scalable source of design-level data for agents that design before they implement, and the round trip measures this without human references.

items.title: The Correctness Gap: Why AI Billing and Prior Authorization Agents Need Enforcement, Not Just Automation
items.abstract: Although artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in the management of healthcare billing, coding, utilization control, and prior authorization, the efficiency of the administrative work does not mean that the administrative actions taken by AI are more accurate or compliant. This paper addresses the correctness gap, that is, the gap between the AI recommendation and the verification needed before that recommendation is implemented. According to previous research in healthcare administration, AI-supported utilization review, and administration governance, proper automation requires controls that ensure the automation is not just capable of performing the recommended task, but also whether the recommended action should be taken. To address this issue, the paper proposes a compliance gate which includes deterministic checks for verifiable requirements, controlled AI judgment on objective criteria in clinical records, and human review for unresolved cases, conflicting evidence, exceptions, and decisions that require human judgment. It also proposes a scoring system of compliance using metric of blocked, missed violation rate, false block rate, escalation rate, time to take the expected action, and estimated cost avoided. This is conceptual and has not yet been evaluated against existing administrative controls. Its purpose is to determine an architecture and an approach to be evaluated by future research rather than claim benefits in compliance.

items.title: THE DEVELOPMENTAL ENVIRONMENT IN PRESCHOOL EDUCATION AND ITS IMPORTANCE
items.abstract: This article discusses the concept of creating a developmental environment in preschool educational institutions, its pedagogical significance, and its impact on children’s development. It analyzes the role of the developmental environment in supporting children’s cognitive engagement, independent thinking, creativity, speech, social and emotional development, and physical activity. Attention is also given to the organization of educational games, didactic materials, creative activity corners, reading areas, and spaces for active games. The article substantiates the need to consider children’s age-related and individual characteristics, ensure safety, provide opportunities for independent activity, and strengthen cooperation between teachers and parents when creating a developmental environment.

items.title: The dissent of decarbonization: Sociotechnical controversies in lithium extraction in the Vale do Jequitinhonha, Brazil
items.abstract: This article describes and analyzes the sociotechnical controversies surrounding lithium exploration in the Vale do Jequitinhonha, Minas Gerais, Brazil, situating them within the context of the global energy transition and the so-called “decarbonization consensus.” The research adopts Actor-Network Theory (ANT) and controversy mapping as a theoretical-methodological approach, making it possible to map the actors, arguments, and disputes that shape the sociotechnical arrangement of lithium mining in the region. The empirical corpus consisted of diverse documents collected through web scraping and monitoring of public debates. The results reveal the conflictual coexistence of antagonistic narratives: on the one hand, lithium as a driver of development, supported by state and corporate discourses that mobilize the idea of overcoming poverty; on the other, mining as a producer of socio-environmental conflicts, denounced by communities, social movements, and researchers. Over time, initial warnings about risks become concrete impacts, broadening the controversy and mobilizing new arenas, such as public hearings, complaints, and legal actions. We conclude that the exploration of minerals demanded by the energy transition, far from being consensual, is traversed by disputes that reveal the production of new sacrifice zones, highlighting the need for more just, participatory, and territorially situated models. By shifting the focus from the “lithium triangle” to the Vale do Jequitinhonha, the article examines a mining frontier that remains little investigated through the lens of controversy mapping.

items.title: THE EFFECT OF VIBRATIONS TRANSMITTED TO AGRICULTURAL TRACTOR OPERATORS' SEATS ON WORKING CONDITIONS AND METHODS OF THEIR REDUCTION
items.abstract: This article examines the sources of mechanical vibrations transmitted to agricultural tractor operators’ seats, their potential effects on working conditions and occupational health, and technical methods for reducing vibration exposure. International standards ISO 2631-1, ISO 5007 and ISO 5008 are considered to establish an assessment framework. Based on a comparative analysis of scientific literature and a simplified mathematical model, an approach to evaluating seat vibration isolation performance is proposed. Particular attention is paid to frequency-weighted acceleration, eight-hour equivalent exposure and seat effective amplitude transmissibility. An illustrative calculation demonstrates how changes in seat vibration levels may affect daily exposure. The numerical example is hypothetical and does not represent original field measurements.

items.title: The Emergence of the Service Techonomy: POPP at the Frontlines and the Rise of AI-Mediated Service Influence
items.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI), data infrastructures, and platform technologies are reshaping services and organizational frontlines. We conceptualize this shift as the emergence of the “service techonomy,” in which omni-personalization manifests via Prescribed, Omnipresent, and Personalized Persuasion (POPP; e.g., such that AI-driven agents guide frontline service interactions, determine service access and offers for consumers, and monitor and steer frontline employees). We derive four functional forms of POPP—interactive, pre-emptive, allocative, and governing—and organize them in a 2 × 2 matrix based on the timing of influence (reactive vs. proactive) and mode of influence (constraining vs. supportive). Anchored in evolutionary economics and the multi-level perspective on socio-technical transitions, our framework shifts attention from isolated technology and personalization features toward broader configurations of AI-mediated influence that shape service value creation, extraction, governance, and potentially inequality across customers, employees, and collectives in service ecosystems. This perspective provides a foundation for future theory building, measurement, and responsible design of AI-mediated services and organizational frontline research.

items.title: The Evolution of Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithms: Structures, Inspirations, and Research Trends
items.abstract: Metaheuristic optimization algorithms have become one of the most important research areas for solving complex, nonlinear, and high-dimensional optimization problems. These algorithms are widely used in many application domains such as engineering, artificial intelligence, energy systems, healthcare, communication technologies, manufacturing, data science, and industrial applications. Their strong exploration and exploitation capabilities enable them to provide effective solutions for optimization problems where classical optimization methods are insufficient. In addition, many metaheuristic optimization algorithms attempt to establish a balanced and adaptive search behavior between exploration and exploitation processes, reflecting an important form of search symmetry during the optimization process. This systematic review presents a comprehensive analysis of metaheuristic optimization algorithms based on 515 distinct metaheuristic optimization algorithms. In this study, the algorithms are systematically classified into eleven major categories according to their inspiration sources and dominant search behaviors: Evolutionary-Based, Swarm Intelligence-Based, Bio-Inspired, Ecological/Environmental-Based, Physics-Based, Mathematics-Based, Human-Based, Game/Sport-Based, Chemical and Molecular-Based, Music-, Art-, and Culture-Inspired, and Hybrid and Advanced Metaheuristics. The review analyzes the historical evolution, inspiration diversity, search structures, symmetry-oriented search balance, and development trends of modern metaheuristic optimization algorithms. This study also provides a broader understanding of how metaheuristic optimization algorithms have evolved structurally and conceptually over time. In addition, the study highlights the importance of balanced and adaptive search mechanisms for maintaining optimization efficiency under complex problem conditions. The findings show that the number and diversity of metaheuristic optimization algorithms have increased significantly, especially after 2015. Population-based search structures remain the dominant optimization approach in the literature, while hybrid optimization methods, adaptive search mechanisms, and artificial intelligence integration have become major research trends in recent years. The study also discusses important challenges in the field, including algorithm similarity, benchmark standardization, theoretical limitations, and fair performance evaluation.

items.title: The Global AI Divide: Infrastructure, Access and Policy Pathways for Democratising Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming more accessible via cloud platforms and generative AI tools. However, the skills needed to develop, manage, and regulate advanced AI are still concentrated in a few countries and major tech companies. This study introduces the emerging Global AI Divide, defined as a capability gap driven by unequal access to compute power, advanced semiconductors, data, capital, energy, models, and specialised human expertise. Through qualitative policy analysis and comparative case studies, it explores the technological, economic, and geopolitical challenges to meaningful AI participation. The research distinguishes between democratising AI creation and democratising AI use, emphasising that wider access to AI applications does not automatically mean true democratisation. It proposes a Six-Pillar Framework for AI Democratisation, covering compute, data, models, innovation, human capability, and governance. The study also points to an emerging policy paradox: expanding fair access to AI while ensuring that advanced frontier systems are developed within proper safety, accountability, and human oversight. Ultimately, it suggests that AI democratisation should be seen as enhancing society’s ability to access, adapt, develop, and govern AI responsibly, not just increasing its consumption.

items.title: The Hand-Proximity Effect in Virtual Learning: How Interaction Design Influences Knowledge Acquisition
items.abstract: Although virtual simulation platforms are widely used in education, they often lack integration with embodied cognition theory. The hand-proximity effect remains underexplored in VR, and how VR design elements mediate it to support higher-order knowledge acquisition is unclear. We manipulated interaction mode, text-hand distance, and virtual hand appearance across three knowledge domains. Results showed that for factual and conceptual learning, neither interaction mode nor text-hand distance significantly affected learning performance. 3D interaction enhanced VR presence but was associated with greater cognitive pressure when combined with far-hand text (p=0.040); anchoring text near the virtual hand mitigated cognitive pressure and improved readability (p=0.005). For procedural learning, realistic human hand models significantly improved learning performance compared to standard cursors (p=0.044). These findings empirically validate embodied cognition in VR and yield guidelines: anchor instructional text in peripersonal space for conceptual learning and use realistic human hand avatars for procedural training.

items.title: The illusion of algorithmic belonging: why generative AI cannot substitute for relational reciprocity in mental health social inclusion
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to critically discuss the fast-moving rollout of generative artificial intelligence (AI) and conversational agents as purported remedies to loneliness and social isolation, analysing the fact that the creation of companionship by algorithms substitutes a one-way connection and fundamentally jeopardises real social inclusion. Design/methodology/approach An interdisciplinary perspective that draws from relational sociology, the social model of disability, critical digital studies and various literatures on psychiatric rehabilitation to critique the inter-personal ethics, psychological dangers and political economy of digital mental health companions. It also comprises a comparative analysis of the existing market leaders in conversational AI. Findings Proximate affective containment is provided by generative AI, but lacks of relational reciprocity, moral agency and shared vulnerability. The replacement of civic infrastructures in community settings by automated, conversational agents can set up a divided mental health system: human-centred relational mental health care for the privileged and synthetic, automated containment for the marginalised service user. Moreover, AI companionship takes out user vulnerability as property information, turns it into a commodity, the lived experience of solitude. Research limitations/implications As a perspective, this paper does not contain empirical data of its own; it constructs the argument by conceptual synthesis instead of a systematic review, and the examples of markets discussed (e.g. Woebot, Wysa, Replika) are illustrative, but not comprehensive or evaluative of current versions of products and so may have changed significantly since the time of writing. Longitudinal studies that compare the outcomes of service users using algorithmic companionship with peer-support and Clubhouse models will confirm the synthetic inclusion construct developed here, and could be used for future research. Practical implications Offers evaluative tools to the mental health commissioners, clinicians and third sector organisations to avoid the “community replacement” trap of digital engagement, keeping AI a cognitive prosthetic and not a substitute for interpersonal interactions. Social implications Disciplines policymakers from adopting techno-solutionism as an excuse for austerity-driven disinvestment of physical community centres, peer respites and inclusive civic spaces and calls for the protection of the human social commons. Originality/value This paper outlines the concept of a “synthetic inclusion” that reveals that the illusion of connection created by conversational AI is a commodity, and that social isolation is structurally reinforced. It contributes to the critique of mental health in the digital age by examining unconstrained large language models from a perspective of surveillance capitalism and intersectionality.

items.title: The image of scientists among neurodivergent children: a pilot study
items.abstract: Abstract This pilot study aimed to explore how a specific group of neurodivergent students in the 4th and 5th grades of elementary school represent scientists through drawing. To this end, the Draw-a-Scientist Test (DAST) was administered to 7 neurodivergent children with a diagnosed Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) who participated in the Young Scientists Project. The analysis of the drawing data was conducted using a multimodal vision-language model (ChatGPT, GPT-4o version) with the prompt “Evaluate the drawings using the Draw-a-Scientist Test checklist”, followed by independent researcher review to ensure consistency and contextual interpretation. Within this small pilot cohort ( n = 7), the drawings predominantly contained visual features commonly associated with traditional representations of scientists, featuring laboratory instruments, a predominantly laboratory environment, and male figures in 6 of the 7 drawings. Representations of scientists in diverse real-world contexts, or utilizing digital technology, books, or chemical formulas, were absent. While strictly illustrative and limited by the small sample size, these preliminary observations suggest a reliance on conventional perceptions of scientific figures among these participants. These preliminary observations warrant further investigation using larger cohorts to evaluate whether tailored, inclusive pedagogical strategies can broaden perceptions of science.

items.title: The Impact of AI on Education and Careers: US Students' Perceptions
items.abstract: The growing use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools in higher education and the workplace has sparked both optimism and concern among educators, policymakers, and employers. These changes directly affect students, but their voices receive less attention than those of faculty members and institutions. This study examines key aspects of student-AI interaction, including familiarity, usage patterns, and perceived career impact. The study used a qualitative design based on semi-structured interviews. Respondents included six undergraduate students in the business administration department of a major state college in Nebraska, USA. The thematic analysis revealed two main themes. The findings suggest that students hold a cautious but positive view of AI. They support clear institutional guidelines and a more deliberate effort to include AI literacy in coursework. The findings have significant implications for stakeholders seeking to enhance learning and prepare students for future careers where AI plays a major role.

items.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence Language Models on Critical Thinking in Theoretical and Practical Aspects of Learning among Undergraduate Nursing Students: A Narrative Review
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) language models are increasingly used in higher education. Many students use them for learning, often without proper academic policies or guidelines. Nursing undergraduate curricula include both theoretical and practical aspects of learning, in which critical thinking is essential, especially for clinical decision-making. This review explores the effects of AI language models on the critical thinking skills of undergraduate nursing students. Sixty-seven articles published between 2020 and 2025 on AI in nursing, medicine, or higher education, and its impact on learning and cognition, were analyzed and synthesized. Findings revealed that AI language models offer benefits, limitations, and ethical concerns. Benefits include improved academic writing, rapid access to information, and support for self-directed learning. Limitations include overdependence, biased content, and reduced social learning. Ethical concerns include confidentiality and plagiarism. In nursing education, AI models affect critical thinking both positively and negatively, enhancing simulated clinical decision-making but potentially reducing independent analysis and interactions with real patients. Studies recommend developing guidelines, training, and balanced integration to maximize benefits while minimizing risks.

items.title: The impact of artificial intelligence on journalism: How media trust and attitudes toward journalists shape acceptance, trust, willingness to pay for AI news, and support for replacing journalists
items.abstract: Although AI is advancing rapidly in many fields, its use in journalism is especially significant, as journalism shapes public opinion and fosters democratic discourse. Artificial intelligence (AI), in particular, has attracted attention for its potential to greatly enhance journalists’ work, but also raises concerns about ethics and job displacement. However, previous research has largely overlooked the public’s perspective on AI, even though understanding these views is crucial for predicting future consumption patterns. This study addresses this gap using data from cross-sectional surveys in Spain ( N = 2337) and Germany ( N = 2213), revealing cautious public attitudes toward AI in journalism. In both countries, acceptance of AI in journalism, trust in its output, willingness to pay for it, and acceptance of AI replacing human journalists are moderate to low. Favorable attitudes toward human journalists positively influence views of AI in journalism, while trust in the media shows a mixed effect. Overall, the findings suggest that public attitudes toward AI in journalism align with broader views on AI, with individual perceptions of AI being a stronger determinant than opinions on media and journalists.

items.title: THE IMPORTANCE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES IN IMPROVING ACCOUNTING IN THE CONTEXT OF THE DIGITAL ECONOMY
items.abstract: This study examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in transforming the accounting system amid the rapid development of the digital economy. The research uses content analysis of the scientific literature, a comparative analysis of traditional and digital accounting, a synthesis of secondary statistical data from international consulting firms, and a descriptive analysis of Uzbekistan’s digital tax platforms. The results show that machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision, predictive analytics and anomaly detection do more than automate accounting tasks: they speed up financial data processing, reduce human error and support strategic management decisions. The discussion addresses the changing role of the accountant and the opportunities specific to Uzbekistan. The conclusion sets out promising directions for the transition from traditional accounting to “intelligent systems” and offers practical recommendations.

items.title: The Issue of Human Resource Training to Meet the Requirements of Developing the Productive Forces in the Current Context of Digital Transformation in Vietnam
items.abstract: Digital transformation is bringing about a qualitative transformation of the productive forces in Vietnam, in which data are becoming a new object of labor, digital platforms and artificial intelligence are emerging as important means of labor, and knowledge is increasingly functioning as a direct productive force. In this transformation, workers continue to occupy a decisive position, while facing competency requirements that differ substantially from those of previous periods. Therefore, human resource training is not merely a social policy accompanying modernization; rather, it constitutes an integral component of the development of the productive forces themselves. This article examines how human resource training can meet the requirements for developing the productive forces within the current context of digital transformation in Vietnam.

items.title: The last human language: Artificial intelligence, translation, and the future of communication
items.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence has transformed translation from a distinctly human linguistic practice into an increasingly automated process. Large language models can translate, paraphrase, interpret, and generate communication across languages with unprecedented speed, raising a fundamental question: if machines eventually become the primary mediators between languages, what happens to the human meanings, cultural memories, and forms of difference embedded within language? Science fiction has anticipated this problem through its recurring fascination with artificial languages, machine communication, alien linguistics, and technologically mediated translation. This article examines Samuel R. Delany’s Babel-17 (1966), China Miéville’s Embassytown (2011), Ian McEwan’s Machines Like Me (2019), and Kazuo Ishiguro’s Klara and the Sun (2021) to examine how artificial intelligence and nonhuman communication destabilize conventional assumptions about language. Drawing upon Walter Benjamin’s theory of translation, Ludwig Wittgenstein’s philosophy of language, N. Katherine Hayles’s posthumanism, and recent scholarship on AI translation and linguistic bias, the article argues that translation is not merely the transfer of information between languages but a negotiation of cultural difference. It proposes the concept of “linguistic posthumanism” to describe a future in which communication is increasingly produced through collaboration between human and artificial linguistic agents. The article ultimately argues that the greatest danger posed by AI translation is not that machines will replace human language, but that they may silently standardize linguistic difference by privileging languages, meanings, and cultural assumptions already dominant within technological infrastructures.

items.title: The Need and Presence of Core Therapeutic Elements in Artificial Intelligence Mental Health Chatbots in Comparison to Human Therapists: A Mixed-method Approach
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) has made significant strides in mental health support, yet its ability to replicate core therapeutic qualities remains limited. Aim: This study aims to explore the need and presence of Rogerian therapeutic attributes of empathy, unconditional positive regard (UPR) and genuineness in human therapists and AI mental health chatbots. Design: This research employed mixed-method approach to compare Rogerian qualities in single-session therapy of young adults ( N = 60) with AI/human therapists. Materials and Methods: A convenience sampling method was employed to recruit participants. Participants’ perceptions of the therapeutic experience were measured using eighteen Likert-scale items (Cronbach’s α = 0.926) based on the core therapeutic attributes of empathy, UPR, and genuineness. Qualitative insights were obtained from open-ended questions. Statistical Analysis: Quantitative data were analyzed for frequencies, Chi-square, and Multivariate analysis of variance using SPSS 21. For qualitative analysis, QDA Miner Lite was used to generate codes and themes and perform Agglomerative Hierarchical Cluster Analysis. Results and Conclusion: Findings indicate that participants perceived human counselors as significantly more empathic and genuine than AI counselors. No differences were reported for UPR. Participants evaluated human and AI therapists along two distinct dimensions: relational depth, which strongly favored human therapists, and functional accessibility, which favored AI. Exposure to AI counseling appeared to increase participants’ willingness to consider AI as a preferred therapeutic modality, although human therapists remained the preferred choice overall. The findings underscore AI’s potential as a complementary tool for low-intensity problems, but reaffirm the irreplaceable value of human therapists in emotionally complex interactions.

items.title: The Next-Gen Commerce Graduate: Thriving in an AI-Driven Economy-An Empirical Analysis of Student Perceptions and Curriculum Relevance
items.abstract: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into global business workflows has fundamentally reshaped employability expectations, requiring modern commerce graduates to possess both analytical and technological capabilities. This empirical study investigates commerce students' perceptions regarding AI adoption, their confidence in entering an AI-driven job market, and the perceived relevance of current higher education curricula. Primary data was gathered through a structured 5-point Likert scale questionnaire administered to N = 150 undergraduate (70%) and postgraduate (30%) commerce students across various specializations. Given the non-normal, ordinal nature of the data, descriptive statistics (Medians and Interquartile Ranges) and non-parametric inferential methods—including Spearman’s rank correlation, the Mann-Whitney U test, and the Kruskal-Wallis H test—were employed for hypothesis testing. The findings reveal that informal or active usage of AI tools does not significantly correlate with perceived career confidence (rs = .138, p = .091). Instead, graduate job market confidence depends strongly on formal institutional curriculum adequacy (rs = .665, p < .001). Comparative analysis showed significant differences in curriculum perception across academic levels (p = .005), with undergraduates expressing greater dissatisfaction than postgraduates. Furthermore, job confidence varied significantly across specializations (p < .001), with Business Analytics students reporting lower confidence (Mean Rank = 43.40) than traditional streams, reflecting heightened critical awareness of industry technical demands. The study concludes that higher education institutions must urgently reform commerce curricula by embedding applied AI applications, automated analytics, and algorithmic decision-making to bridge the gap between academic preparation and workforce expectations.

items.title: The perception of craft construction workers on the application of artificial intelligence in health and safety in UK construction
items.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is starting to play a bigger role in health and safety (H&S) in UK construction. While most studies today are concerned about managerial perceptions, technological possibilities and organisational readiness, there is a dearth of research on the use of AI based on the lived experiences of construction workers. This research aims to explore how craft construction workers perceive the application of AI in construction H&S. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative research design was used to garner the data to achieve the research aim. Overall, 20 craft construction workers with 5–20 years of experience were purposively selected from the UK (England, Scotland and Wales) and interviewed. The data were analysed using thematic analysis. Findings The findings revealed a slow but gradual uptake of AI-enabled H&S tools, and AI is mostly used for hazard warning on construction sites. Some workers view AI as a beneficial modern addition; others perceive it as a form of surveillance. In addition, workers’ age influenced their attitudes towards AI, and the clarity of AI tools’ functions influenced how workers accepted them. One benefit of AI is hazard detection, but workers lack trust in its reliability. Practical implications The findings reported in this study will assist the construction industry, policymakers and technology developers in addressing concerns about AI in H&S while leveraging the benefits associated with their usage. Originality/value This study is among the first qualitative studies to empirically explore the perspective of key stakeholders (frontline workers−craft construction workers) in the UK on the application of AI in construction H&S management. This study contributes to future AI adoption in construction H&S management in the UK.

items.title: The Psychology of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists: Evidence for Distinct Effects on Reward, Interoception and Cognition
items.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are widely used for obesity and type 2 diabetes, supporting weight loss and glycaemic control through effects on appetite and ingestive behaviour. The psychobiological mechanisms underlying these effects remain unclear. We reviewed evidence for candidate mechanisms and analysed quantitative and qualitative self-reported changes in appetite-related experiences from 704 people using GLP-1 RAs. Participants reported multiple changes that appeared distinct for food versus alcohol, with reductions in food urges and cravings largely independent of changes in alcohol use. Enhanced awareness and utilisation of hunger and satiety signals were frequently described, suggesting potential changes in interoceptive processes. Changes in enjoyment of eating were largely independent of reductions in food cravings, urges to eat, and gastrointestinal side effects. Improved ability to eat in a goal-directed manner was also frequently reported. Results support the presence of multiple cognitive and behavioural processes contributing to reduced food intake and provide testable hypotheses to explore in experimental work designed to isolate effects of GLP-1 RAs on goal-directed control, interoceptive awareness, attention, memory, and executive function.

items.title: The Role of Agentic Instruction Categories for Code Generation: A Study of Five Python Libraries
items.abstract: This replication package contains the datasets, artifacts, and analysis materials for the paper “The Role of Agentic Instruction Categories for Code Generation: A Study of Five Python Libraries”. The package includes the selected Python library datasets, generated agent files, reconstructed library variants, evaluation results, structural metrics, token-usage records, and analysis scripts used in the study. The study evaluates five instruction categories—Repository Overview, Function Description, Implementation Detail, Testing, and Reconstruction Steps—across all 31 non-empty combinations using two LLMs and five Python libraries. The materials support reproduction of the agent file and code generation cost analysis, compilation evaluation, functional-correctness evaluation using human-written tests, and structural-similarity analysis reported in the paper.

items.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Optimizing Renewable Energy System
items.abstract: The growing transition to renewable energy sources, such as solar, wind, hydro, and geothermal, presents significant challenges due to their intermittent nature, requiring advanced optimization strategies for efficient integration into existing power systems. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative tool in addressing these challenges by enhancing energy forecasting, optimizing smart grid operations, and improving predictive maintenance. This study employs a secondary research methodology, conducting a qualitative analysis of existing literature, case studies, and technical reports on AI applications in renewable energy optimization. The study explores how machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and reinforcement learning (RL) enhance energy forecasting, real-time grid management, and fault detection. AI-driven models improve the accuracy of solar and wind energy predictions, allowing better supply-demand balancing. Additionally, AI-powered smart grids enhance energy distribution, reduce wastage, and increase grid reliability. AI also enables predictive maintenance, minimizing operational costs and infrastructure failures. The research is grounded in Systems Theory, Optimization Theory, and Technological Determinism, offering a structured framework for analyzing AI’ s impact on renewable energy systems. Despite its advantages, AI integration faces challenges such as high implementation costs, data privacy concerns, and infrastructure compatibility issues. By reviewing real-world case studies, the study demonstrates AI’ s effectiveness in optimizing renewable energy systems, emphasizing its potential to accelerate the transition toward a more sustainable and resilient energy future.

items.title: THE ROLE OF SYNTACTIC ANALYSIS IN NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING AND COMPUTER LINGUISTICS
items.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and digital communication has significantly increased the importance of technologies capable of processing human language. Every day, large volumes of textual information are generated through websites, scientific publications, social networks, digital libraries, and electronic communication platforms. Analyzing this information efficiently requires computational methods that can identify not only individual words but also the grammatical relationships that connect them. Natural language processing (NLP) has emerged as an interdisciplinary field that combines computer science, linguistics, statistics, and artificial intelligence to address these challenges.

items.title: THE ROLE OF TEACHER SCAFFOLDING IN AI-ASSISTED EFL WRITING INSTRUCTION
items.abstract: The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) education has created new opportunities for supporting students’ academic writing. AI-powered tools can provide immediate feedback, suggest vocabulary alternatives, and help learners identify grammatical and organisational problems. However, the effective integration of these tools requires more than technological access. Teachers play a crucial role in helping students interpret AI-generated suggestions, maintain their own ideas, and use digital resources responsibly. This paper explores the role of teacher scaffolding in AI-assisted EFL writing instruction through a conceptual analysis of relevant literature. It examines how structured guidance, modelling, guided practice, and reflective activities may help learners engage more critically with AI-generated feedback. The paper proposes a four-stage instructional approach consisting of teacher modelling, guided evaluation of AI suggestions, independent revision with appropriate support, and reflective assessment. Particular attention is given to maintaining the balance between technological assistance and the development of learners’ writing competence. The discussion suggests that teacher scaffolding can provide an important pedagogical foundation for integrating AI into writing instruction without replacing human judgement or teacher–learner interaction. The proposed approach may inform the design of AI-assisted writing activities in higher education EFL contexts, including Uzbekistan. Further empirical research is required to assess its effectiveness in classroom practice. Keywords: artificial intelligence, teacher scaffolding, EFL writing instruction, AI-assisted learning, pedagogical guidance, academic writing.

items.title: The samplr package: A tool for modeling human cognition with sampling algorithms
items.abstract: Many models of cognition have sampling as a central component. Researchers have used them to explain human performance across a wide range of tasks involving perception, probability reasoning, and choice. One family of these models takes inspiration from sampling approaches developed in statistics, either by adjusting samples with prior beliefs or by implementing a sampling algorithm that overcomes the difficulty of independent samples at the expense of autocorrelation. While these models have been successful in modeling human behavior, their adoption has been slowed by the technical difficulties in applying them. Here, we introduce the samplr package, which includes a variety of these algorithms and cognitive models built upon them. We show how models in this package can match qualitative patterns found in human data, and walk readers through examples of how to compare these models quantitatively to human data. This tool aims to make these methods accessible to many more researchers.

items.title: The study of Chinese EFL teachers' emotions in the digital transformation of education
items.abstract: Introduction The rapid and continuing development of digital technologies has significantly reshaped the educational landscape, generating diverse emotional experiences among teachers. This study examined the emotional experiences of Chinese EFL teachers and the major antecedents of those emotions. Methods This study employed an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design. First, questionnaire data collected from 296 university EFL teachers identified five primary emotions (love, joy, anger, sadness, and fear). Secondly, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 16 participants to explore the antecedents underlying these emotional experiences. The qualitative findings were subsequently integrated with the quantitative results and presented through a joint display. Results The findings showed that EFL teachers experienced positive emotions more frequently than negative emotions. Of the five primary emotions, joy and love had the highest mean scores, followed by fear, anger, and sadness, respectively. The findings further showed that teachers' emotions were closely associated with their professional goals and students' performance. Several antecedents were found to shape these emotional experiences. The flexibility, interactivity, and innovative opportunities introduced by digital transformation enhanced EFL teachers' sense of love for their work. Likewise, the efficiency and abundance of resources provided by digital tools and platforms contributed to their sense of joy. In contrast, students' misconduct and dishonest behaviors often provoked feelings of anger. Teachers experienced sadness when confronted with students' lack of critical thinking and when they felt inadequately supported in their work. Fear was primarily driven by peer pressure, time constraints, and the threat of being replaced by artificial intelligence. Discussion The study discussed the implications of these findings and proposed recommendations for emotion regulation and emotional support for EFL teachers in China and comparable educational contexts.

items.title: The Synthetic Imputation Approach: Using LLMs to Generate Synthetic Texts for Underrepresented Categories in Supervised Classification Tasks
items.abstract: Abstract Annotated text data are central to many empirical applications in political science, yet many annotation tasks involve categories that are sparsely populated. These low- N categories pose problems for both encoder-only and decoder-only (generative) Transformer large language models (LLMs), leading to low performance, biased evaluation and measurement error in downstream analyses. This article introduces the synthetic imputation approach, a targeted method for expanding sparse categories while remaining consistent with the category-defining content of the human-coded examples. The approach uses a generative LLM to produce additional texts for underrepresented categories by conditioning on small, rotating subsets of human-coded examples. Rather than paraphrasing or replacing the original data, synthetic imputation adds informative variation only where data are thin. I evaluate the approach using both encoder-only and decoder-only LLM classifiers across multiple political science applications. The results show that synthetic imputation substantially improves performance and evaluation stability in sparse settings, recovering full-sample performance once a modest number of true observations is available, with limited and predictable overfitting at very low levels of N .

items.title: THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES IN TEACHING INFORMATICS
items.abstract: This article explores the opportunities for using artificial intelligence technologies in teaching computer science and examines their potential impact on educational effectiveness. AI tools can support personalized learning, explain complex concepts, improve programming skills, provide automated feedback, and reduce teachers’ routine workload. The article also discusses important challenges, including data privacy, information security, academic integrity, and the reliability of AI-generated content. Practical recommendations are proposed for integrating artificial intelligence into computer science lessons in a responsible and pedagogically effective manner.

items.title: The World Won't Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can solve complex interactive tasks, yet reasoning and tool calls take time. In continuously changing environments, an otherwise correct action may arrive too late. We introduce RealtimeBench, with 180 tasks across six game types, to evaluate agents while games continue running during inference. Paired evaluations show that GPT-6.1-sol outperforms the faster Jev when games are paused, but falls behind when they keep running. We propose Two-Timescale Offline Recursive Self-Improvement (TORSI): a slow teacher studies failures and tests corrections in paused games between attempts, then writes reusable instructions for a fast student. The student acts without teacher calls during gameplay, and validation scores determine which updates are adopted. Two rounds raise Jev's average test score from 13.51 to 24.19 on a 0--100 progress scale, improving all six game types. The instructions also improve average scores for three other models without retuning. These findings point toward real-time intelligence: enabling powerful LLM agents to remain effective in a continuously changing world by organizing deliberation, learning, and action across timescales.

items.title: THEORETICAL AND METHODOLOGICAL FOUNDATIONS FOR DEVELOPING THE PROFESSIONAL-METHODOLOGICAL COMPETENCE OF PROSPECTIVE ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEACHERS THROUGH THE INTEGRATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND ADA
items.abstract: The digital transformation of higher education necessitates the reconsideration of approaches to preparing prospective English language teachers. In this context, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and adaptive learning technologies represents a promising direction for developing professional-methodological competence, enabling future educators to design learner-centred instruction, differentiate educational content, analyse learning progress, and select appropriate pedagogical strategies. This article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations of competence development through the integration of AI-supported tools and adaptive learning environments. It synthesises competence-based, learner-centred, constructivist, and technology-enhanced learning approaches to establish a conceptual framework for teacher preparation. The proposed framework comprises five interrelated components: motivational and value-based, cognitive, technological, operational-methodological, and reflective-evaluative. Particular attention is given to the relationship between AI literacy, pedagogical decision-making, adaptive instructional design, and professional reflection. A phased methodological model is proposed, encompassing diagnostic assessment, personalised learning, AI-supported methodological practice, teaching simulation, and reflective evaluation. The article also addresses ethical considerations, including data privacy, algorithmic bias, academic integrity, and the importance of maintaining teacher autonomy. The findings provide a theoretical basis for designing university-level teacher education programmes that respond to the demands of digital transformation.

items.title: Think Once, Reflect Twice: How Feedback Shapes Human-AI Collaboration
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly supports human decision-making in high-stakes domains, designing effective human-AI collaboration becomes critical. Successful collaboration requires humans to reflect on decision-making processes and adjust their strategies accordingly. Current research typically investigates interventions, such as explainable AI, that target reflection during the decision-making process (reflection-in-action). Less attention has been given to retrospective examination of decisions (reflection-on-action). This work explores reflection-on-action by studying the impact of feedback on reliance behavior and human-AI team performance. Specifically, we investigate feedback interventions targeting overrides of AI advice through a behavioral study (N=244). We find that such feedback influences reflection-on-action, while unidirectional feedback risks reducing subsequent reflection-in-action. Furthermore, we identify opposing shifts in reliance behavior that leave overall human-AI team performance unchanged but show context-dependent effects. Balanced feedback did not show these risks, preserving both concurrent and retrospective reflection, offering insights for designing for appropriate reliance on AI.

items.title: Thinking in Graphs: Neo4j-Backed Exploit-Chain Reasoning for LLM Penetration-Testing Agents
items.abstract: LLM coding agents such as Claude Code and OpenAI Codex can drive penetration-testing tools, but they reason about an engagement as a flat list of findings in a context window. Attackers think in graphs: isolated low-severity exposures turn catastrophic once chained through credential capture, privilege escalation, and lateral movement. This gap feeds a common belief that AI agents cannot truly chain exploitation; we argue this describes the flat context window, not the model. We present ChainGraph, a pattern that externalizes exploit-chain reasoning into a Neo4j property graph wired to an off-the-shelf agent via the Model Context Protocol, no bespoke harness. Findings, attack steps, credentials, assets, and tamper-evident evidence receipts are typed nodes with pre/post-condition edges; JSON/Markdown holds documentary memory while Neo4j holds reasoning memory. We formalize five operator questions (next-step inference, entry-to-crown-jewel pathing, combined-severity promotion, evidence provenance, and chokepoint identification) as reusable Cypher and Graph Data Science queries, plus a chain-severity score distinct from per-finding local severity. On a synthetic multi-forest Active Directory engagement modeled on GOAD, in live Neo4j with GDS, three findings rated Medium in isolation become Critical once their path to the forest root is materialized, and betweenness centrality names the best chain break-points. Scoping each decision to a graph result rather than re-reading the engagement cut the reasoning payload by about 98% on a token proxy. We give a reproducible setup for Claude Code and Codex. Results are illustrative single-run measurements, not a benchmark.

items.title: Threads of tomorrow: Reddit’s conversation on generative AI across the fashion domain
items.abstract: Generative AI is spreading across the fashion industry, yet public discourse about these tools remains understudied. We analyze 15,854 Reddit posts (January 2022–June 2025) using BERTopic modelling and transformer-based sentiment analysis. Through human topic screening, we identify nine fashion-related themes containing 4836 documents of theme-level analysis. Apparel design generates the most discussion and one of the highest shares of negative sentiment, revealing a ‘democratization paradox’: AI expands access to design but still requires professional refinement. Sentiment also differs by application type, with instrumental uses, such as virtual try-on and personal styling, attracting significantly less negativity than representational uses, including avatars and AI personas. Ethics discussions are dominated by AI undressing tools, a concentrated harm pattern that emerged nearly two years before the TAKE IT DOWN Act. These findings extend technology acceptance frameworks and demonstrate how social media discourse can provide early warnings of emerging risks while guiding fashion practitioners and policymakers.

items.title: TimeRSI: Towards Self-Improved Agentic Deployment for Time-Series Foundation Models
items.abstract: Time-series foundation models provide strong zero-shot forecast, but deployment for real-world applications still requires task-specific designs for model inputs and outputs. Direct inference can leave domain knowledge and recurring forecast errors unaddressed, while tailored pipelines require substantial human expertise and effort. We introduce TimeRSI, a self-improving agentic deployment system around frozen forecasting models. A coding agent translates task descriptions into executable pipeline changes. It tests each revision on historical forecasting windows and uses observed errors to guide subsequent revisions. During deployment, an adaptive selector chooses among the resulting pipelines using completed forecasts under similar conditions. Across 198 tasks on TIME and fev-bench, TimeRSI outperforms all submissions on six point and probabilistic forecasting metrics. Controlled comparisons support the value of feedback-guided revision over non-iterative pipeline search. Further experiments verify the generalization with different coding agents and forecasting models. Code is available at https://github.com/haoxin1998/TimeRSI.

items.title: TMT attention to technological innovation and AI invention: Evidence from Chinese listed firms
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a central field of corporate innovation, yet firms differ substantially in the extent to which they develop AI inventions. Drawing on upper echelons theory and the attention-based view, this study examines whether top management team (TMT) attention to technological innovation is associated with firms' subsequent AI invention and which organizational pathways are consistent with this relationship. Using a multi-source panel dataset of Chinese listed firms, we measure TMT attention to technological innovation from the Management Discussion and Analysis sections of annual reports and measure AI invention using AI patent applications filed by the listed firm. The results show that TMT attention to technological innovation is positively associated with subsequent AI invention. Further analyses provide evidence consistent with pathways through collaboration with universities and research institutes and AI human capital readiness, whereas internal R&D investment does not emerge as a significant pathway. We further compare AI invention with broader digital invention. TMT attention to technological innovation is also positively associated with subsequent digital invention, and research collaboration remains a significant indirect pathway, whereas internal R&D investment and digital human capital readiness do not. Additional tests show that the indirect effects through research collaboration and human capital readiness are significantly larger for AI invention, while the R&D pathway does not differ significantly across the two domains. These findings suggest that AI and broader digital invention share organizational foundations, but external scientific knowledge and specialized human capital are more strongly associated with AI invention.

items.title: Tools versus rules: School leaders as protectors of collective professional capital under the shock of generative AI
items.abstract: This qualitative study of 17 educational leader candidates interrogates how future administrators negotiate generative artificial intelligence's (GenAI) disruptive insertion into P-12 school activity systems. Framed by the integrated lenses of Professional Capital theory and Cultural-Historical Activity Theory (CHAT), the research traces systemic contradictions between rapid algorithmic capabilities and lagging institutional rules, professional norms, and layered, entrenched divisions of labor. Data were generated via open-ended pre and postcourse surveys during a graduate leadership preparation course in summer 2025, intersecting with an acute macrohistorical shock: the public popularization of an MIT Media Lab preprint warning of GenAI causing student “cognitive debt.” Baseline findings reveal severe primary and secondary contradictions characterized by an acute fear of automated deprofessionalization, curriculum deskilling, and the depletion of teacher decisional capital under rigid district policies. However, post-intervention reflections indicate microlevel movements along an expansive learning cycle. When leadership preparation intentionally mobilizes social capital through collaborative theoretical reflection, candidates shift from defensive, rule-bound policy enforcement toward critical AI literacy. Ultimately, this article offers a conceptual framework for leadership preparation programs to buffer school ecosystems against external narrative panics, resolve institutional friction, and sustain human professional capital against automated erosion.

items.title: Toward AI-Enabled Precision Exercise: Neurophysiological Effects of Acute Moderate-Intensity Resistance Exercise on Executive Function in College Students with Different Motor Skill Backgrounds
items.abstract: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and intelligent healthcare technologies, integrating neuroimaging with exercise interventions has emerged as a promising strategy for promoting cognitive health and precision medicine. This study investigated the immediate effects of acute moderate-intensity resistance exercise on executive function in college students with different motor skill backgrounds and explored the underlying neural mechanisms using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). Furthermore, the multimodal behavioral and neurophysiological data generated in this study provide a valuable foundation for future AI-assisted cognitive assessment and precision exercise prescription. A total of 36 healthy male collegiate athletes were recruited and assigned to either an open-skill group (n = 18) or a closed-skill group (n = 18). Participants completed a 30-minute acute moderate-intensity resistance exercise session at 70% of their 10-repetition maximum (10RM). Executive function was assessed before and after exercise using the Stroop task, 2-back task, and More-odd shifting task to evaluate inhibitory control, working memory, and cognitive flexibility, respectively. Simultaneously, changes in oxygenated hemoglobin (ΔHbO 2 ) within the prefrontal cortex were continuously recorded using fNIRS. Data were analyzed using paired-sample t-tests and two-way repeated-measures analysis of variance. The results demonstrated that acute moderate-intensity resistance exercise was associated with significant improvements in selected executive-function outcomes within both groups. In the open-skill group, reaction time decreased in the Stroop task, while accuracy increased and reaction time decreased in the 2-back task. In the closed-skill group, reaction time decreased in the 2-back task. Both groups showed improvements in selected outcomes of the More-odd shifting task. However, no significant Group × Time interactions were observed for any behavioral outcome, indicating that the magnitude of behavioral change did not differ significantly between groups. fNIRS findings revealed task- and channel-specific changes in prefrontal ΔHbO 2 following exercise. Moreover, significant Group × Time interactions in ΔHbO 2 were observed at selected prefrontal channels during the Stroop, 2-back, and More-odd shifting tasks, suggesting that motor skill background may be associated with different patterns of prefrontal hemodynamic response following acute exercise. In conclusion, acute moderate-intensity resistance exercise was followed by improvements in selected executive-function outcomes in young male collegiate athletes. The integration of behavioral assessments with fNIRS-derived neurophysiological data provides additional evidence regarding behavioral and prefrontal hemodynamic responses to acute resistance exercise. Although the behavioral changes did not differ significantly between groups, exploratory fNIRS findings indicated task- and channel-specific differences in ΔHbO 2 changes between the open-skill and closed-skill groups. Further studies incorporating a non-exercise control condition, larger and more diverse samples, and appropriate correction for multiple channel-level comparisons are needed to confirm these findings.

items.title: Toward explainable traffic crash liability analysis via neural-symbolic multimodal reasoning: Integrating visual perception with legal knowledge graphs
items.abstract: Determining traffic crash liability relies on rigorous on-site evidence and legal provisions and involves substantial manual intervention and potential human error. However, intelligent traffic monitoring systems focus on detection and tracking and cannot provide structured, rule-grounded decision support for formal crash-liability analysis. Moreover, emerging multimodal large language models (MLLMs) suffer from object hallucination that distorts or omits physical evidence, and their opaque reasoning cannot produce explicit evidence-to-rule chains required for traceable and reviewable liability analysis. This paper proposes CrashLex, an explainable neural-symbolic decision-support framework that integrates visual perception with legal knowledge graph reasoning to align multimodal inference with predefined statutory rules and traceability requirements. Within CrashLex, a dual-query vision-language architecture employs parallel semantic and symbolic streams to mitigate object hallucination, utilizing Scene Queries for global context modeling and Perception Queries for fine-grained atomic feature extraction, respectively. The domain-specific legal knowledge graph maps these atomic facts from observable physical conditions to corresponding statutory elements, providing a structured basis for rule-grounded assessment. A logic-driven aggregation protocol then imposes explicit constraints derived from extracted facts and statutory provisions onto the inference process, thereby enabling traceable and interpretable preliminary liability assessment. On the held-out DeepAccident benchmark, CrashLex achieves a Legal Accuracy of 94.0% under the fixed legal-output evaluation protocol and an Object Hallucination Rate of 2.8%, corresponding to an 82.1% relative reduction from the 15.6% rate of the best-performing MLLM baseline on this metric. CrashLex grounds its assessment results in the deterministic execution of predefined legal rules rather than relying solely on unconstrained probabilistic generation, providing verifiable reasoning chains for rule-grounded human review.

items.title: Toward Healthcare System Digital Mission Engineering: A Multilevel Health Informatics Framework for AI Integration, Demonstrated Through Cardiovascular Risk Management
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly operates within interconnected healthcare information systems, but governance remains model-centered and weakly tied to institutional mission. Healthcare System Digital Mission Engineering (HSDME) adapts digital mission engineering to treat the mission, rather than an application or model, as the primary system of interest. The framework links three architectural levels through six stages, fourteen tasks, and a bidirectional governance and quality-assurance thread. Two nested cardiovascular cases illustrate system-level adoption of the 2026 dyslipidemia guideline and encounter-level reuse of the resulting architecture. Structured author-led walkthroughs assessed specification completeness, consistency, traceability, and reuse; deployment and clinical effectiveness were outside their scope. An illustrative cascade analysis compared Type A (no AI-enabled functions under the HSDME rubric), Type B (pathway-level AI), and Type C (AI-enabled functions in the shared pipeline or governance layer under common system-level controls). With stipulated parameters, greater integration raised decision yield and closed-loop evidence return while increasing human-review burden; no configuration dominated. HSDME contributes a mission-derived multilevel architecture, the three-type AI-integration typology, differentiated evidence routing, and a governed organizational boundary with typed information provenance. It positions health informatics as a coordinating discipline for mission, computable knowledge, interoperable pipelines, and accountable decision support.

items.title: Towards Agentic Robots: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness
items.abstract: Foundation models are driving a paradigm shift in robotic intelligence, moving beyond low-level action prediction to goal-directed orchestration of data collection, model training, task planning, and real-world execution. We characterize this emerging paradigm as an agentic robots, in which agents reason over human instructions, interact with robotic environments, rectify execution errors autonomously, and dynamically adjust operational strategies. Although this field develops fast, current studies are not well connected. Researchers have no consistent view of how to combine different agentic functions into a complete robot system. This paper provides a unified overview of existing research on agentic robots. We first trace the development from robot policies to agentic systems, covering vision-language-action models, world models, and world-action models. We then clarify the definition and scope of agentic robots and organize existing research into seventeen categories across four functional domains: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness. Across these domains, we examine how agents shape model learning and robot decisions, collect and curate robot data, construct worlds, tasks, and tests for learning and evaluation, and organize capabilities for robot use. Finally, we discuss open challenges and outline directions for future research. Looking forward, we hope this work contributes to a clearer understanding of agentic robots and supports new approaches to making them more capable, reliable, and adaptive.

items.title: Towards Efficient Threat Intelligence Instruction Tuning via Quality-Aware and Optimal Transport-Guided Data Selection
items.abstract: High-quality data is essential for improving instruction tuning in threat intelligence analysis. However, existing methods for generating cybersecurity instruction data lack reliable quality assessment mechanisms, and gradient influence-based data selection methods primarily focus on single-sample matching, failing to cover diverse and complex security capabilities. To address these issues, we propose CTI-TDS, a Targeted Data Selection method for instruction tuning in Cyber Threat Intelligence analysis. Specifically, we first filter high-quality CTI instructions by integrating instruction style consistency and security knowledge verification. Furthermore, we formulate gradient influence as a distribution alignment problem, learning a gradient subspace of target tasks and applying entropic regularized optimal transport to optimize distribution matching between training samples and target tasks, enabling diversity-aware data selection. We conduct extensive experiments on CTIBench across multiple large language models. Experimental results demonstrate that when fine-tuning with only a small set of high-value instruction data, CTI-TDS outperforms existing data selection methods and achieves competitive performance on threat intelligence analysis tasks.

items.abstract: The article presents the results of an action-research project that aimed to model and validated the contributions of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) AI as a learning resource in the core curricular lines of the social work formation process. The research responds to the need to model the inclusion GenAI as a learning resource in the university training of disciplines focused on human connection such as social work . Worked with a section of 18 students from the fourth semester of the course, selected by non-probabilistic sampling for convenience A cycle of four work sessions with GenAI was carried out, which was compatible with the training activities of the theoretical-methodological curricular lines of Social Sciences and theoretical-practical social work carried out in the selected subject. The expected results were oriented towards obtaining definitions with GenAI support, collation reflections, GenAI support in writing professional documents and methodological mapping. The validation of GenAI as a learning resource is concluded, with support from teachers and students. In addition, it is confirmed that social intervention occupies a central place in vocational training, which displaces AIGen from an assessment of centrality initially assigned by the digital native student generations, towards a limited and complementary contribution position that adds to the repertoire of available learning resources.

items.title: Training the Next Generation of Future Surgical Residents: A Scoping Review and Proposal for an Undergraduate Curriculum From the Italian Polispecialistic Society of Young Surgeons
items.abstract: AIM: The transition from medical school to surgical residency is marked by a persistent gap between theoretical instruction and clinical readiness. In Italy, variability in training programs across centers creates persistent gaps in residents’ medical education. Scientific societies are asked to identify current training gaps and define the core competencies required for effective surgical training. We propose an undergraduate curriculum to support last-year medical students in Italy.METHODS: A scoping review of the literature focusing on structured surgical curricula for undergraduate medical students was conducted. A suggested “curriculum” was introduced at the 2025 Congress of the Italian Polispecialistic Society of Young Surgeons (SPIGC) in Bari, Italy.RESULTS: The SPIGC curriculum includes seven domains: (1) soft skills: communication, informed consent, and interdisciplinary collaboration; (2) clinical and diagnostic skills: outpatient clinic management and perioperative care; (3) hygiene, prevention, healthcare systems; (4) technical skills; (5) emergency and trauma surgery; (6) perioperative management, integrating Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocols, nutritional assessment, and infections; (7) evidence-based medicine and recommendations. The SPIGC curriculum highlights the importance of simulation labs, hands-on workshops, and online learning, while providing clear pathways for fellowships or masters. It also introduces artificial intelligence (AI) systems as a modern learning tool, while highlighting the importance of their safe and responsible use.CONCLUSIONS: The SPIGC curriculum may provide a structured plan to improve surgical education for medical students in Italy and to align it with international standards. Its acceptability and impact on training quality and patient outcomes remain to be evaluated through future consensus and prospective studies.

items.title: Trans-Vatabnet: Transcriptomic Signatures For Parkinson’s Disease Detection Using Deep Learning
items.abstract: The early detection of Parkinson's disease (PD) is critical for timely and effective clinical intervention and disease management. High dimensional gene expression data redundancy features, class imbalance and limited interpretability are challenges discussed for transcriptomic-based diagnostic approaches. To overcome these drawbacks, TransVaTabNet, new approach that combines transcriptomic analysis, deep learning and explainable artificial intelligence detect PD and discover biomarkers. The RNA-seq data is first pre-processed by low expression gene filtering, Trimmed Mean of M-values normalization, and voom transformation. The differentially expressed genes (DEGs) are determined through the framework of Limma-voom, and are then subjected to stage-specific gene analysis and functional enrichment to map the disease-related biological pathways. The high dimensional gene expression profiles are learned to a compact latent representation using a Variational AutoEncoder, and SMOTE is used to deal with class imbalance. The derived features are then classified with a TabNet model that adopts a sequential attention mechanism to attend to informative transcriptomic patterns. In addition, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) are used for model interpretability and biomarker identification. Experimental results on the GSE216281 RNA-seq dataset are shown to validate the proposed framework with 90.95% Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC), outperforming the classical machine learning models. The results show that TransVaTabNet can provide an accurate, interpretable and biologically meaningful framework for stage-specific detection PD and biomarker discovery, which can support precision diagnosis and further clinical decisions.

items.title: Transforming Financial Management: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Society is evolving and so too (finally) are the plans of modern financial institutions. This is because corporate sustainability has moved away from business as usual and is instead utilized to grow competitive advantage by increasing choice for employees and power-with stakeholders to pursue non-traditional routes. This makes robust financial management in the financial industry imperative to uphold sustainable practices and advance. Successful financial management now combines its primary duties with artificial intelligence (AI) to monitor, evaluate, and execute projects within the time constraints set. A few important credit decisions made during the growth or expansion of credit options were significantly improved using an array of AI techniques in this case. This method is so well used by finance managers that they have the ability to watch over all of their offices or a single transaction within any part of them.

items.title: Tratamiento de datos personales mediante inteligencia artificial en plataformas digitales
items.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence models and systems capable of acting semi-autonomously has exacerbated issues relating to the processing of personal data, profiling and automated decision-making. The average user is unaware of the true extent to which their personal information is processed, what data is collected, how long it is retained, for what purpose it is used, or which third parties may access it. This situation leads to a gradual loss of effective control over personal information and calls into question the adequacy of consent as the primary mechanism legitimising data processing. This phenomenon is particularly significant on everyday digital platforms such as Spotify, where artificial intelligence plays an essential role in generating music recommendations, personalising content and developing behavioural profiles through the continuous analysis of activity carried out within the platform.

items.title: Trust in voice-based assistants: a multidimensional conceptualization based on in-home user interviews
items.abstract: Voice-based assistants (VBAs) such as Alexa and Siri are widely used in everyday life and increasingly act as information intermediaries. Their human-like voices and behaviors can elicit social responses, while new assistants based on large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT voice mode, further blur the boundaries between machine and human communicators. Despite risks associated with misinformation and limited data transparency, adoption remains high. Trust may be relevant to users’ relationships with conversational AI, but there is little consensus on how it should be conceptualized. Technical, interpersonal, and media trust frameworks may all be applicable. This multi-method qualitative study examined users’ subjective concepts of trust through 22 in-home interviews complemented by observational tasks involving participants’ own VBAs and ChatGPT voice mode. Participants drew on interpersonal concepts when defining trust but commonly restricted trust in VBAs to particular tasks and functions. Technical and media-related trustworthiness criteria were especially prominent, whereas social responses and anthropomorphic qualities did not necessarily translate into interpersonal trust. Experience, calibrated expectations, selective use, habitual engagement, and trust were described as closely interrelated. Although ChatGPT was often evaluated positively, particularly as an information intermediary, its perceived capabilities were not uniformly accompanied by greater trust compared with participants’ familiar VBAs. Based on these findings, we propose a preliminary conceptual framework of task-specific hybrid trust in VBAs.
